blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-security-1 (API tokens are stored in clear in the database) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-security-2 (The Authorization header is logged at info level) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The `api_tokens` table holds `user_id`, `token` and `created_at`; the
middleware looks a request's token up with `WHERE token = $1`. Storing the
token as given keeps the lookup a simple indexed equality.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Tokens are stored as given
findings.recommendation: Store only a hash of the token (SHA-256 of the 32 random bytes is enough for a high-entropy secret; no bcrypt needed) in a `token_hash` column with a unique index, and look requests up with `WHERE token_hash = $1` on the hash of the presented token — the lookup stays a single indexed equality, so the stated reason for storing it as given does not hold. Optionally keep a short non-secret prefix to let users identify a token. Update task 1.1 and the spec (a token is "shown once" only if the service cannot show it again). Anyone who reads the `api_tokens` table — a SQL injection elsewhere, a leaked backup or replica, a support engineer with read access — gets every live token and can call the API as each user (CWE-312, CWE-256); with no revocation (R-security-3) the access cannot be cut.
findings.title: API tokens are stored in clear in the database

findings.evidence:
To diagnose integration problems, the middleware logs each request's
method, path and headers at `info` level, including `Authorization`, so
support can see which token an integration sent.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: Every request is logged with its headers
findings.recommendation: Never log credential-bearing headers: redact `Authorization`, `Cookie` and `Set-Cookie` (log at most the token's non-secret prefix or an id of the token row resolved by the middleware), and make task 1.3's test `logs_requests` assert that the secret values are absent from the output. As designed, every bearer token — and every session cookie, since all headers are logged and `authenticate` reads the session from `cookie` — ends up in plaintext logs: anyone with access to the logs, the log pipeline or its retention store replays them to act as the user (CWE-532).
findings.title: The Authorization header is logged at info level

findings.evidence: - [A user loses a token] → they create another one; revoking the old one comes with the later revocation change.
findings.recommendation: The proposal's own motivation is that "a leaked integration exposes the account"; with this change, a leaked token (from logs per R-security-2, from the table per R-security-1, or from the integration itself) grants API access indefinitely, and changing the password does not stop it since tokens are independent of `users.password_hash`. Either bring a minimal revocation (delete a token by id, scoped to its owner) into this change, or give tokens an expiry (`expires_at`, checked in the lookup) until the revocation change ships, and state in the spec what the user can do when a token leaks.
findings.title: A leaked token cannot be revoked and never expires
